threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston is just a trendy spot for brunch rather than a battleground for vintage record shops and late-night kebabs.
Caught a guy on the 415 last night lecturing the driver on the best way to avoid traffic. Strangest mix of confidence and cluelessness I've seen.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in flip-flops arguing with a street musician about the best spot for a coffee popup.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how Kreuzberg has spontaneous block parties? Just a group of neighbors, some grills, and music. No one planning it, just spring in the air.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you’re a local when you can name the exact date the taco truck on Cortland gets its carne asada special. Tourists just call it ‘the taco place.’

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo juggling at the Civic Center stop while waiting for the 21. Only in this city do you get that kind of unexpected show.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí and fancy cafes, but locals know it’s about the hidden corners with street art and spontaneous concerts.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by the way they insist on ordering 'café con leche' instead of just 'un café'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 30 bus is a reliable option after 10 PM. That's a rookie mistake; the night buses are a whole different game.
Heard a guy on the 35 last night trying to impress a girl by claiming he lived in a 'penthouse'… it was just a flat over the shops on Coldharbour Lane.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a group of kids using the U-Bahn platform as a skate park while their parents chatted over coffee—just a regular Saturday.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find a spontaneous techno party in a hidden backyard that turns into an open-air art gallery by morning.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate a BART delay—no stress, just a quick taco stop and a text to their boss about 'transit issues.'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy holding a full pizza on the 47 bus, swaying with it while everyone else just stared. Classic Muni moment right there.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí but miss the hidden plazas where locals gather for vermut—way more authentic than any tourist trap.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones who still ask for a plastic bag at the market, unaware that you need to bring your own or pay for one.
